hook: SCP-400 is a body-horror entry about parasites that make use of dead infants and the parents who love them. Content note: it describes in clinical detail insects burrowing into babies, the corpses being breastfed for months, and injuries to a mother's body. The most affecting part is an interview with one mother, so take it slowly.
whyItMatters:
The horror here is built from one of the strongest human instincts, the urge to care for a child, and turns it into the creature's food supply and its defense. The cognitohazard is what lets the premise work: nobody under the effect can see what is wrong, so love itself becomes the cover.

It also shows the clinical tone doing heavy lifting. Week-by-week figures, entry points and hormone levels are given in the same flat voice as the containment rules, and that calm makes the content harder to read, not easier.
thingsToNotice:
The life cycle section works like a timeline: an infant stops breathing within forty minutes, starts moving again hours later and slowly dries out while the parents see a healthy baby, and by week twelve the bugs crawl out to induce pregnancies in the mother so that she gives birth to dozens more, which is worth keeping in mind when you reread the procedures, especially the order to watch for drops in daycare enrollment and the plague cover story.

Mrs. B's interview is the heart of the file. She insists her boys are three months old though the date shows over two years have passed, starts to mention a doctor who came to the house and then loses the thought, and the post-interview exam finds worse damage to her than to any other host mother. The addenda end coldly: her twins survive five years in Foundation custody as long as they are fed, one is dissected after an experimental supplement stops it, and the parasites' pheromones turn out to resemble the Foundation's own amnestics.
